headline: intg-prod-a1: cause not established — setroubleshootd at 99.7% CPU correlates with batch latency and console slowness; audit log evidence is outstanding and convergence is blocked
known: Process snapshot at 2026-03-17T19:00:00+00:00 shows pid 3501048 (setroubleshootd, user audit-analysis) at 99.7% CPU with 79h 58m cumulative CPU time, started 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00.
SELinux is confirmed in enforcing mode; denials are real and being logged.
Integration service JVM (pid 3489339) is at 5.6% CPU and 24.8 GiB resident set at snapshot time.
Memory series shows a rising sawtooth pattern beginning 2026-03-02T00:00:00+00:00, with memory climbing approximately 3.5 GiB over roughly 15 hours then dropping sharply, repeating each cycle.
13 memory exhaustion problems (P-4100 through P-4112) opened in the 03:00–04:00 UTC window and auto-closed approximately 2.5 hours later each night over 15 days.
All 13 problems are unacknowledged; the observability platform notes no problem in this window was acknowledged, assigned, or actioned.
CHG-88104 records installation of endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27 on 2026-02-22.
The audit-analysis-server package has been installed on this host for 3 years; the 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 event is an activation, not an installation.
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1.
No JVM heap or thread dump has been collected from pid 3489339.
User-reported symptoms are batch transfer latency and console slowness.
suspected: SUPPORTED — setroubleshootd is consuming approximately 100% CPU in response to a high-volume stream of SELinux AVC denials that began 2026-03-02, and this CPU saturation is the proximate cause of batch transfer latency and console slowness on intg-prod-a1. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denial counts per hour from 2026-03-02 onward; if denial volume is low or absent, setroubleshootd CPU consumption has a different cause not yet identified. Contradicting evidence: no direct observation of AVC denial volume or rate exists; the audit log is outstanding, so the link between setroubleshootd CPU consumption and a denial storm is inferential.

PLAUSIBLE — installation of endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27 (CHG-88104) on 2026-02-22 triggered novel SELinux AVC denials that activated setroubleshootd on 2026-03-02, initiating the CPU and memory exhaustion pattern. CHG-88104 is the only change record in the pre-onset window per the change correlator (confidence: plausible). Registry caveat: self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true — the agent may have self-updated between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-02, which could explain the 8-day gap between installation and onset. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denials from 2026-02-22 through 2026-03-02; if no denials are attributable to the endpoint-compliance-agent source domain, this hypothesis is falsified; additionally, confirm whether the agent was active and consuming memory between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-01, as flat memory during that period weakens the correlation. Contradicting evidence: the 8-day gap between agent installation and onset weakens temporal proximity; no AVC denial log has been collected to confirm the agent is the source domain; the version running at onset may differ from 7.4.2-27 with no registry evidence.

PLAUSIBLE — the integration service JVM has a memory leak contributing to the rising sawtooth memory pattern, with the JVM's resident set growing during each batch cycle and partially recovering, compounding memory exhaustion alongside setroubleshootd. This hypothesis cites prior incident INC-2411, which described memory exhaustion on an integration-class host with a JVM workload; divergence: INC-2411 had a recorded heap configuration change, which is absent here. Falsifying test: collect a JVM heap dump from pid 3489339; if heap occupancy is stable and within historical norms, the JVM is not contributing to the memory growth pattern; swap metrics would also clarify whether the JVM is being paged out during exhaustion events. Contradicting evidence: JVM CPU is only 5.6%, inconsistent with a runaway workload driving memory growth; the sawtooth reset pattern (sharp drop) is more consistent with a process restart or GC event than a leak, which would typically not recover without intervention; the current 24.8 GiB reading is elevated above the 23.1 GiB steady-state baseline but not dramatically so.

SUPPORTED — recurring nightly memory exhaustion events (P-4100 through P-4112) have been auto-closing without acknowledgement for 15 days, masking a progressive degradation that has now manifested as user-visible latency. This hypothesis cites prior incident INC-2419, which described the same signature and auto-close behaviour and ran 10 days unacknowledged before action; divergence: INC-2419 was resolved by restart without establishing cause — that outcome must not be repeated here. Falsifying test: compare batch transfer completion times and console response times on days when problems were open versus closed; if performance is identical in both states, the auto-closing events are not causing user-visible impact. Contradicting evidence: auto-close could reflect genuine recovery if the batch workload completes and memory is released; the pattern alone does not confirm suppression of a worsening condition.
outstanding: Audit denial log for the affected window, showing source domain and denied action for each denial — requested from platform_team 149 minutes ago, still not received. Obtain /var/log/audit/audit.log from intg-prod-a1 covering 2026-02-22 through present and extract AVC denial counts per hour and source domains. This is the deciding evidence; convergence is blocked until it is received.

standing_conditions: Integration service JVM on intg-prod-a1 holds 23.1 GiB resident of 32 GiB total RAM as steady state for at least 6 months, with no alerting configured and no owner assigned. This leaves only approximately 8.9 GiB free at baseline, meaning any additional persistent process (such as setroubleshootd at 622 MB) materially reduces the margin before memory exhaustion. This condition did not cause the incident but explains why a new consumer was able to trigger exhaustion.

13 memory exhaustion problems (P-4100 through P-4112) fired and auto-closed over 15 days with zero acknowledgements, zero assignments, and zero actions taken. The auto-close behaviour created a false impression of self-resolution and allowed a progressive degradation to reach user-visible impact undetected. Alerting configuration and on-call response procedures for auto-closing problems on this host require review as a post-incident finding.

The non-production equivalent host (intg-nonprod-a1) has build_parity=false with a different patch level and different installed agents. This means the non-prod environment cannot be used to safely reproduce or test hypotheses about production behaviour without accounting for these differences.

The change registry has a confirmed blind spot: self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true. Agents that self-update do not produce package records, meaning the current running version of any self-updating agent on this host may differ from the registry without any audit trail. This is a standing gap in change visibility for this host.
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1; any application-layer change delivered outside the pipeline is invisible to the change registry. This is a standing gap in change traceability.

Authorisation is required before any restart action.
